Independent replicate fits of the empirical Bayes switching model (different latent draws). Monte Carlo run r uses replicate r mod 3, so the Monte Carlo error of the fitted hyperparameters is carried into the projection; their spread, and each replicate's standard errors, are reported in projection_report.json.

How the projection treats the estimated hyperparameters (delta, beta_d, tau_u). 'laplace': every run draws them from the truncated normal approximation of their posterior under a flat hyperprior on the bounds (the curvature of the marginal likelihood at the optimum), and then draws each country's effects from their posterior at those values, so estimation uncertainty in the hyperparameters is carried into the projection (Kass and Steffey 1989). 'plug-in' conditions on the estimate, the usual empirical Bayes choice, which understates uncertainty.
Replications of the parametric simulation study of the switching estimator (run.py recovery).

Concentration of the Dirichlet-multinomial likelihood of the survey switching rows. A row carries the information of at most about alpha respondents, which allows for survey design effects and for the model's simplifications (one conversion effect per country, converts placed by local prevalence). alpha = 30 and 100 fit the evidence equally well and 300 worse (marginal likelihood); infinity would be the multinomial.

status: estimated range (calibrated to UN foreign-born stocks 1990-2020)
source_or_reason: Two-way circulation beyond WPP net migration, fraction of population per year, scaled by each country's mobility. religion_forecast/backtest.py (foreign_born_check) starts from the UN 1990 foreign-born stocks and simulates 1990-2020 at the central parameters: with no extra circulation the simulated world total is 254 million against the UN's 252 million in the modelled countries, and the population-weighted and country-mean errors are lowest near 0.0002 (0.99 and 3.07 pp, against 1.04 and 3.27 at 0); at 0.0004 every error is larger than at 0. The range spans the two optima. (Before migration volume was preserved under soft margins, the same test favoured slightly higher values.) Gross flow estimates (Abel & Cohen, about 0.0016 per year) are higher because many movers return: the model counts a returning emigrant as foreign-born in their own country, so it needs the lower, stock-consistent rate. Gross churn is therefore understated; foreign-born stocks are not.

How strictly the flow solver enforces WPP's net migration against the observed migrant network: flows F = a K b with a = (E / K b)^rho and b = (I / K' a)^rho. rho = 1 enforces both WPP margins exactly; WPP's projected margins are partly inconsistent with the network (for example Pakistan keeps emigrating about 0.5-1 million a year while Gulf net immigration falls to almost zero after 2030), which then forces emigrants into whichever countries have positive net immigration (Pakistan would supply 46% of UK immigrants in 2020-2050 against 8% of its 2020 foreign-born). Lower rho lets both margins give way. The 1990-2020 corridor test in religion_forecast/backtest.py (migration_corridor_check.csv) fits destinations' origin mixes best near 0.75; the range spans that uncertainty. The world total of flows is kept at the requested total, so rho moves flows between corridors and countries but does not reduce how many people migrate (an earlier version lost about a fifth of all migration at rho = 0.75).
Weight of geography versus existing migrant networks in new flows, when bilateral stocks exist. 1.0 = gravity only (used without the UN table).

status: assumption (range), with the minority effect re-estimated at its centre
source_or_reason: Upper bound on a religion's emigration propensity per person, as a multiple of its origin's average (religion_forecast.migration.minority_selectivity). The minority effect share^-lambda is otherwise unbounded: a small minority in a country with large emigration then emigrates at many times the national rate and is drained within decades (in an earlier version Christians in Pakistan fell from 1.3% to 0.4% by 2050 and made up 14.5% of Pakistan-born migrants), which no census shows. The one origin-country figure available, Christians 16% of India-born migrants (Pew 2024) against 2% of India, is reproduced at 11% with a cap of 3 and 17% with 6 (20% uncapped). The calibration of kappa and lambda (religion_forecast.calibration.calibrate_affinity) is done at the centre of the range; every run draws its own cap. Pew's migrant file by country of origin would identify it directly.

Optional limit on an origin's share of a destination's arrivals, as a multiple of its share of that destination's migrant stock (religion_forecast.migration.cap_corridors). The 1990-2020 corridor test (data/validation/migration_corridor_check.csv) fits worse with any cap from 1.5 to 4 at every margin softness, and observed arrivals were more concentrated by origin than the uncapped model simulates, so no cap is applied. Large projected corridors such as Pakistan to the United Kingdom therefore come from WPP's projected national margins and are reported as such.

No country is assumed to hold a fertility advantage for centuries.
